ASICS reports 60% faster misplaced-inventory recovery with Corvus One

A new Mississippi warehouse results report describes 26 misplaced cases found in three months, with staff resolving drone-identified discrepancies.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Operational results from a warehouse

ASICS America and Corvus Robotics reported results from the 855,000-square-foot Byhalia, Mississippi distribution center, including 60% faster recovery of misplaced inventory. This story focuses on reported operating results, not a claim that drone use just began: an earlier Corvus guide already discussed this site.

Night scans and human reconciliation

Drones scan locations, read UPC codes and count boxes for comparison with warehouse records; staff review discrepancies the following morning. The report describes seven nightly flights totaling about 19 hours. In the returns/singles and case-reserve areas, counting rose from twice yearly to monthly, a sixfold increase that should not be generalized to the entire warehouse.

Reading the figures carefully

Over three months, the system helped locate 26 misplaced cases containing more than 200 pairs of shoes. About 200 labor hours per month were reportedly redirected to exception resolution and root-cause work. The 60% figure concerns recovery speed, not a 60% labor reduction. These are customer and supplier reports, not independently audited findings.
